I stayed for 2 days at Vaishali Inn and found the experience below expectations considering the price. The room felt outdated and was quite small, with a very small TV (around 28 inches) barely visible from the bed. Basic amenities like hand wash were missing—only a bar soap was provided. While the staff was polite and helpful, the overall facilities were lacking. Breakfast was average. Not worth the price for the quality offered.

I initially booked my stay for two nights but ended up extending it for four more, which speaks to my overall positive experience. The hotel’s location is excellent—very close to the metro station, making it convenient for commuting. Additionally, there are several markets nearby, and the locality itself is quite good. As for the hotel, it is decent and provides a comfortable stay. The room I was given was spacious with a well-sized bed. One of the highlights is their in-house restaurant, which serves purely vegetarian food. I tried the sandwich and pasta and both tasted quite good. The hotel staff were courteous and helpful adding to the pleasant experience.

I had a wonderful stay at Hotel Emporio Grand. The rooms were clean, comfortable, and well-maintained. The hospitality here truly stands out. I would especially like to mention Mr. Vishnu, who was extremely courteous and helpful throughout my stay. His warm and professional approach made me feel very welcomed and comfortable. He went out of his way to ensure everything was taken care of with a smile. Highly recommend this hotel for anyone looking for excellent service and a pleasant experience.

I recently stayed at The Emporio Grand (or insert the actual name here), and I must say it was an outstanding experience from start to finish. The hotel's location is very convenient close to public transport, shops, and restaurants making it ideal for both business and leisure travelers. The room was spacious, clean, and well-appointed. The bed was comfortable, the linens were fresh, and the bathroom had all modern amenities working properly. The housekeeping staff did a prompt job every day, which added to the comfort. What impressed me most was the staff everyone from the reception desk to the dining area was warm, courteous, and eager to help. They responded to requests with a smile and genuine helpfulness. The food was flavorful, and the breakfast spread had a good variety both local and international options which made mornings a treat. For the price paid, the value is excellent. The hotel offers luxury without the exorbitant rate, so you truly feel that you get more than what you expect. Overall, I highly recommend The Emporio Grand to anyone visiting the area if you want comfort, good service, and a memorable stay. I would definitely stay here again.

Review by Dr. Hukam Singh Sandu on Hotel Tara Palace, Daryaganj I recently had the pleasure of staying at Hotel Tara Palace in Daryaganj with my best friend, and the experience was truly commendable. From the moment we arrived, the staff was warm and welcoming, ensuring a smooth check-in process. The rooms were well-maintained, clean, and comfortable, offering a peaceful ambiance perfect for relaxation. The hotel’s location is ideal, with easy access to nearby historical sites and markets. One of the highlights of our stay was our meeting with the hotel owner, who was incredibly hospitable and passionate about providing quality service. He personally ensured that our needs were met and even shared insights about the hotel’s commitment to guest satisfaction. The food quality was excellent, with a variety of delicious and hygienic options available. The overall atmosphere was pleasant, and the services exceeded our expectations. Whether for business or leisure, Hotel Tara Palace is a great choice for anyone visiting Daryaganj. I would highly recommend this hotel for its exceptional hospitality, cleanliness, and affordability. Looking forward to visiting again! Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)

Gunjan, who was our server during breakfasts was very attentive and made great recommendations. Overall it was a great hotel experience. Highly recommend!

I recently stayed at Hotel Park Plaza, Shahdara, and overall, it was a very pleasant and comfortable experience. The staff, housekeeping team, and reception deserve a special mention — they were warm, attentive, and ensured that I was well taken care of throughout my stay. Every request was handled promptly, and their professionalism truly added to the comfort of my visit. That said, there are a couple of areas where I feel the hotel can significantly improve. The quality of food stands out as the biggest opportunity — both variety and taste could be enhanced to match the otherwise high standards of the property. A more diverse menu and better flavour profile would go a long way in elevating the overall guest experience. Additionally, the hygiene of the common areas needs attention. The carpets appear worn-out and dirty, and certain spots — especially around the windows in the restaurant — have noticeable dust accumulation. Improving cleanliness in these shared spaces will greatly enhance the ambience and first impression. Overall, it was a comfortable stay with great service, and with a few improvements in food quality and common-area hygiene, the hotel can truly shine.

Overall experience Zero professionalism No transparency in billing Extremely rude and irresponsible reception staff Mental harassment, especially while staying with parents and students ❌ I would strongly NOT recommend this hotel to families, parents, or students who expect basic respect, honesty, and proper billing practices.

review_text: Extremely Disturbing Experience – Unacceptable Staff Behaviour My experience at Hotel City Park, Pitampura was deeply disappointing and distressing. The behaviour of two staff members, Mr. Akram and Mr. Joginder Chikkara, was rude, arrogant, and completely unprofessional. At the time of checkout, we were virtually held hostage for nearly 50 minutes, being accused of stains on the room carpet. When I reasonably questioned how it could be established whether those stains were present prior to our check-in—especially since no photographic evidence was shown to us—the situation escalated unnecessarily. If the hotel is so sensitive about its carpets, basic documentation at check-in should be a standard practice. Shockingly, we were asked to step out of our car, taken back to the room, and made to wait while the staff started cleaning the carpet themselves, turning the entire situation into a melodrama. Meanwhile, my family—including elders—was left waiting in the car for almost an hour, which was completely unacceptable. When I asked how long we would be kept in this hostile situation, Mr. Joginder and Mr. Akram responded arrogantly, stating that we would not be allowed to leave until the carpet dried. Having stayed at multiple 5-star properties across India, I can confidently say I have never witnessed such rude, humiliating, and customer-hostile behaviour. Adding to this ordeal, the food quality was extremely poor and appeared stale. Disturbingly, two members of my family had to rush to the hospital with symptoms of food poisoning, which raises serious concerns about hygiene and food safety at this property. Such conduct by staff not only destroys the spirit of customer centricity but also serves as a strong word of caution for future travellers. I sincerely request Mr. Agarwal, the owner of the property, to take stringent and visible action against such behaviour so that it serves as a lesson for the entire staff and prevents other guests from going through a similar experience. Highly disappointed. Would strongly advise travellers to exercise caution before choosing this hotel.

review_text: Extremely Disappointing and Unsafe Stay Experience at Fab PP Residency I am writing to formally express my deep dissatisfaction with my recent stay at Fab PP Residency as a solo female traveler. I had booked a room via an online platform using a temporary ID and paid the full amount upon arrival at hotel scanner. I reached the property at 9:30 AM, as I had important work scheduled by 10:30 AM. I requested early check-in, understanding that it may depend on availability. However, the staff asked me to wait in what can only be described as a cluttered, unsanitary storage room — where staff members were eating and garbage was piled. Feeling extremely uncomfortable, I chose to wait outside. After a long wait, even when rooms were ready, I was not provided with a clean or proper space to get ready. I was briefly given a ground-floor room where the electricity was not functioning due to MCB issues. I had to request repeatedly before they made any effort to address the issue. Eventually, I was asked to vacate that room, and my luggage was moved while I waited again. They temporarily offered me access to a different room to use the washroom — it was filthy and sandy. I explicitly informed the staff to arrange a clean and proper room before I returned. When I came back after two hours, a room was finally allotted. I used it for only 2–3 hours to freshen up and left without staying overnight due to how uncomfortable and unhygienic the room and surroundings were. The bed was uncomfortable and dirty. The washroom was in poor condition, and the entire atmosphere was dark, messy, and uninviting. The behavior of the receptionist and staff throughout was extremely unprofessional, lacking both basic hospitality and courtesy — especially unacceptable for solo female travelers. This was the worst hotel experience I’ve ever had, and I hope necessary action is taken to ensure no other guest goes through such a disappointing and distressing stay. Sincerely, Chitra

Horrible Experience – Avoid at All Costs! I stayed at Hotel Tara Palace for an entire week, and I deeply regret it. The only reason I stayed that long was because I had to be within Chandni Chowk, and switching hotels was a hassle. If that hadn't been the case, I would have left immediately. First off, the service is abysmal. The staff is ill-mannered and rude, with no regard for customer service. As a solo female traveler, I would never recommend this place to anyone—it felt anything but safe or accommodating. The rooms are disgusting. They have a horrible, damp smell, and the bed sheets and mattresses are old and stinky. The pillows are no better. The rooms were never cleaned on time, and when they finally were, the job was half-hearted. There are no electric kettles provided, and while some rooms have working TVs, many do not. Basic amenities like fans don’t work properly, which is unacceptable, especially during the peak summer heat in India. When I complained about the fan not working, the staff had the audacity to tell me I should have checked it before agreeing to the room! The manager's attitude was beyond rude. The hotel is undergoing renovations, but it doesn't excuse the fact that the lift is old and unreliable, unable to carry much weight. The rooms are not suitable for three people, even though they may try to squeeze guests in, which is just misleading. The worst part of my stay was how dismissive the staff was towards complaints. I asked for hot water because I wasn’t feeling well, and after requesting it twice within an hour, I was treated as if I were being a nuisance. Room service was consistently late, and the staff seemed annoyed at every simple request. They kept asking for IDs repeatedly, which felt suspicious and unprofessional. Overall, this hotel is a disaster, especially for the price they charge. The management is haughty, rude, and refuses to acknowledge or apologize for their poor service. I would never stay here again and absolutely do not recommend it to anyone.

What adds to the appeal is the heritage feel of the architecture, which sets it apart from modern glass-and-steel hotels. Many guests also appreciate the colonial-era ambiance, as this property (Maidens Hotel, built in 1903) is one of Delhi’s oldest luxury hotels, offering a blend of history and modern amenities. It features an outdoor pool, a fitness center, and a charming courtyard café, making it not just a stay but an experience steeped in tradition.

If you are anxious about travel to Delhi with a toddler who has never set foot in the country, this is your place to be. My toddler ate all the meals here, drank their RO purified water, and even had some cut salads and fruits and did well with no health issues. What made the whole experience absolutely fantastic was the hospitality. Everyone was very professional, pleasant and just happy! The restaurant also modified food and made some dishes for my toddler and offered to pack food for my kid's journey out of Delhi. The grounds are massive and we spent so many hours just walking around. It also felt less smoggy than rest of the city. My special thanks to the GM Prachi ji, Jashan Ji, Sudhanshu ji and all the staff for being so kind and accommodating our needs. I cannot imagine staying anywhere else in Delhi. Thank you! PS: Not all rooms have windows that open to the outside. I would suggest to call ahead to book one.

I would like to add a disclaimer that this is a review for the staff, specifically the front office and the supervisor of that night, Rachit Verma, as they merit one. We arrived shortly late at night due to unforeseen slowdowns during our travel and rushed to check in. Unfortunately, our troubles of the day continues as we realized that we made our booking on the wrong day... one month in advance. The hotel was already at full capacity and we were greatly disappointed. Despite the situation, the staff was exceptional in making sure we were given guidance and attention during this time. We managed to find another booking quickly and this would have escalated to something dismal were it not for the staff's patience and experience. We were definitely looking forward to spending time in the Maidens Hotel as it is a terrific location. We will surely make another attempt during travels to India's capital city. This time, with proper dates and knowledge that a stellar staff is there to provide us with quality service.

A really nice surprise, possibly the best service I have ever experienced at any hotel before. It will be difficult to stay anywhere else in Delhi and it will be the new benchmark to compare other hotels too. ⭐ 1/5 — Worst Hotel Experience. Completely Unprofessional & Mismanaged. I stayed at Dusky Hotel & Restaurant during my exam at M.A. Global Examination Centre, Sector 22 Rohini, and the stay was honestly pathetic from start to finish. ❌ Scam in Pricing When I reached, the board clearly said “Rooms @ ₹600”, but on call, the owner told me the room was ₹1500. After reaching, I found out rooms were actually available for ₹1200 and even less. It genuinely felt like they took advantage because I travelled all the way from Punjab and urgently needed a room. The receptionist made excuses that cheaper rooms were “booked”, but only 2 rooms were actually occupied. ❌ Dirty Room & Terrible Washroom The room looked fine from outside, but: • Washroom was extremely dirty • Commode was broken • Washroom lock was jammed • Sink had hair • Bedsheet had holes • The room was not cleaned after previous use • Only one old towel provided • No soap, no shampoo, no water—not even basic amenities • A glass was kept which was full of dirt I asked them to clean the sink; they barely removed the visible hair. That’s it. ❌ Unprofessional Behaviour Later the owner called and instead of listening, he: • Accused us of “troubling” the staff • Said he would believe his employee over me • Told me to “go stay at Radisson” if I wasn’t satisfied • Argued even after I said the room wasn’t clean I had already paid ₹500 online, and he acted like refunding was doing me a favour. ❌ Morning Comment From Owner In the morning, while I was checking out, the owner said to me: “You studied in a different room, I didn’t say anything… you used two rooms.” I had only sat in another room for barely 1–2 hours because the chair in my room was broken and leaned all the way back, making it impossible to study. He still counted that as “using two rooms”. ❌ Zero Knowledge & No Basic Supplies There was not even handwash in the bathroom. When I asked, the receptionist gave us a fabric perfume mixed with water as “handwash”. My father immediately pointed out that it didn’t even lather. This shows their lack of basic knowledge and hygiene. ❌ Mosquitoes, Smell & Poor Location • The room was filled with mosquitoes; me and my father barely slept. • The tap water smelt like sewage—we had to buy water bottles to brush. • The location is extremely poor and unsafe. • A big dirty water pond is right in front of the hotel. • The area is underdeveloped, and even delivery guys struggle to find it. • No market nearby at all. ❌ Overall Except for the four walls, everything else was below basic standards. This was a “no choice” situation because of my exam, or I would never have stayed here. 👉 I strongly do NOT recommend this hotel to anyone. There are better and safer stays on the other side of the area with proper markets and better access. Never staying here again. Forgot to click pictures of the room and the washroom. This is a below-average hotel, and rooms are easily available on a walk-in basis at very low prices. However, some online platforms list it at highly inflated rates (above ₹1500), which is not justified. I would strongly advise against booking through such platforms. Despite being associated with the Fab group, the property does not meet FabHotel standards and appears to be priced at a much higher level than the quality offered. Amenities are basic and below average. Rooms are not very clean, and there is no in-house restaurant for dining, although room service is available. Service quality is average at best. Overall, the value depends entirely on how much you pay and the purpose of your stay. If you only need a place to sleep overnight—for example, during exams—it is acceptable, provided you do not overpay. A reasonable price would be in the ₹500–₹1000 range, and on some online platforms it is even available for ₹300–₹400, which feels more appropriate for this property. I don't know how they are able to maintain such a good rating on Google Maps.

Okay I will write this review in detail: 1. Decor/party hall: It's a nice hall without any pillars in between which can certainly interrupt the view of the people sitting there. Let's come to the main part, catering, I was expecting that it's in posh area of Rohini so, catering must be good. But here they lost all of their scores. Let's start with drinks! They offered me Lemonade, their was no spice in it, nothing for the sake of taste, it was too bland in taste. I had ask the manager their to add few spices in it to make it good. He did the change and came back with another version which was good. After that I tried few starters, french fries was all tangled up with each other they were not fine crispy potato fingers we eat at other cafes, let's not talk about McDonald's here. They were not even close to our homemade fries. Next thing was chilly paneer. It was like they just fried the paneer and toasted in some capsicum and onion. They were not at all chilly, and I don't think they even coated the paneer cubes with corn flour or maida at all. Which gives them some texture before the tossing part comes in. After that I was saving my remaining taste buds for the main deal. I tried chole, they were nice, kadhi it was again too plain, no spices, just enough sour to hide away all other things. No chilly tempering, no kadhi pata, nothing. I tried mix veg which was okay. Zeera rice was too oily u can feel the oil in the serving dish, breads was fine soft and fresh. In salad there was no cucumber, beetroot as if they are cutting budget in everything. Malai kofta was nice with some sweet texture, dal makhni was not even close to any place u can say. It was just plain black dal cooked. So overall, you can book the place but please give them detailed instructions about the food, or better you can ask for some tasting. I missed this. Suggestion to the banquet: Change your chef, he is not worth keeping! Change him may be you will get more business. Because you really have nice place, you just need nice food. He really don't have any idea about party caterings. I gave three stars all based on location and decor.

Amazing place for a relaxing stopover! I visited MHOne Resort on the Delhi–Karnal Bypass (GT Road), and it genuinely exceeded my expectations. The moment you walk in, the interior décor instantly grabs your attention. The ambience is modern, elegant, and surprisingly well-maintained — perfect for both family trips and long-route travellers looking for a comfortable break. The food is another highlight. Freshly prepared, flavourful, and served with good portion sizes. Whether you’re grabbing a quick bite or sitting down for a proper meal, the quality really stands out. Their service staff is polite and attentive, making the dining experience even better. The overall property is clean, spacious, and well-organized. Highly recommended for travellers who want comfort, good food, and a premium feel without any hassle.

We recently hosted a wedding function at MH1 Banquet near GT Karnal Road, and unfortunately, our experience was extremely disappointing and stressful. From the beginning, there was a clear lack of professionalism and transparency. Even after finalizing the package and signing the contract, we were repeatedly pressured for additional payments during the event for services that were already agreed upon. This constant demand for extra money created unnecessary tension and embarrassment in front of our guests. The rooms promised for the bride and close family members were not handed over on time, causing chaos during the preparation hours. Despite repeated follow-ups, the management showed no urgency or accountability. One of the most serious issues we faced was regarding the liquor arrangements. Several bottles that we had arranged were stolen during the event. The stock kept reducing without explanation, and when we questioned the staff, there was no proper response or investigation. This resulted in financial loss and extreme frustration for us as hosts. The behavior of some waiters was highly unprofessional. They kept interrupting guests repeatedly and, in some instances, directly demanding and even snatching money in the name of tips. This created a very uncomfortable environment and left many of our guests shocked. We had coordinated with the person handling the jaimallaplannerz, named Gaurav, who had promised certain decorations and commitments at the time of booking. However, he completely backed out of what was promised once the event began. The arrangements were not as discussed, and several agreed points were ignored. Even after the contract was signed, he demanded additional money at the last moment, putting us under pressure during the function. We also relied on the event vendors and panel services recommended by the banquet management, but we felt misled. There were hidden charges, poor coordination, lack of commitment, and a clear difference between what was promised and what was delivered. Once payments were secured, service standards dropped significantly. Other major issues included: • Rude and dismissive responses when complaints were raised • Delays in food service and inconsistent food quality • Lack of cleanliness in certain areas • Poor coordination between management and ground staff • Repeated last-minute financial demands • No accountability for missing items Overall, this was an extremely stressful and upsetting experience for our family. A wedding is meant to be a joyful and memorable occasion, but due to the mismanagement, broken promises, and constant financial pressure, it became a source of regret. We strongly advise future clients to be extremely cautious, document every commitment clearly, and monitor arrangements closely before trusting this venue.

I have visited many banquet halls across Delhi NCR, but MH One Resort Hotel in Alipur, Delhi stands out as one of the largest, offering multiple venue options. Its main banquet hall is particularly impressive-spacious and beautifully designed. However, the breakfast was quite ordinary and delayed by one to two hours, indicating that the staff on duty need better training and coordination. The dinner in the main hall, on the other hand, was excellent, with a wide variety of starters, chat stalls, and numerous dessert options. Overall, it was a pleasant experience.

It is with profound disappointment that I pen this review regarding the resort that was entrusted with hosting my brother-in-law’s wedding ceremoney— an occasion meant to embody joy, elegance, and seamless hospitality. Regrettably, the experience was an egregious departure from all reasonable expectations. The culinary arrangements were distressingly substandard; the food lacked freshness, flavour, and basic quality, rendering much of it inedible and ultimately wasted. Such negligence in catering is inexcusable for an event of this magnitude. Equally disconcerting was the resort’s hospitality, which reflected a palpable absence of professionalism and attentiveness. The staff appeared indifferent, inadequately coordinated, and, at critical moments, conspicuously unresponsive to repeated requests for assistance. More troubling was their reluctance to acknowledge concerns or engage in constructive dialogue, leaving guests feeling disregarded and inconvenienced. A wedding is not merely an event but a cherished memory in the making. Unfortunately, the resort’s mismanagement, lack of accountability, and deficient service overshadowed what should have been a celebratory and graceful affair. I would strongly urge prospective patrons to exercise caution and seek assurances of service quality before committing to this venue for any significant occasion.

review_text: Rating: 0/5 (If that were possible) If you value honesty, transparency, or basic ethics, do NOT book Mantram for any important function—especially something as meaningful as an engagement. I was crystal clear about my budget from DAY ONE. Not once. Not twice. EIGHT separate times I explicitly asked them to confirm that the costs would not exceed my budget only then I will come and discuss anything. Every single time, I was reassured with sweet words, fake confidence, and vague promises like “don’t worry, we’ll manage within this.” And what did I get in return? A final quotation that exceeded my agreed budget by a shocking 8 LAKHS when my grandmother was in hospital - they made me drive 4 hours just to tell me how I cant afford them because they lied to me in the first place. Yes. ₹8,00,000. That’s not a “small mismatch.” That’s not a “miscommunication.” That’s called dishonesty, plain and simple. If you know you cannot deliver within a budget, have the decency to say so upfront. Instead, Mantram chose the classic trap: • Lure you in with false assurances • Let you emotionally commit to the venue This is not professionalism. This is manipulation.
